name: tnf-fate-in-space
title: TNF fate in space
description: What decides whether a cell survives or dies when TNF reaches it by diffusion, and does space act only through the dose that arrives, or also through when it arrives?
question: What decides whether a cell survives or dies when TNF reaches it by diffusion, and does space act only through the dose that arrives, or also through when it arrives?
hypothesis: Map each run with a diffusing TNF bolus onto the uniform-dose curve by the TNF dose that reached the cell (peak and time-integrated). If fate collapses onto that curve, space acts only through dose; if it does not, arrival timing matters. NF-kB's nuclear wave timing under the moving front is the mechanism either way. Every coupling is first calibrated (Study 0) on parts verified by the workspace's compose-api checks.

studies.name: s0-coupling-calibration
studies.title: Coupling calibration (NF-kB switching speed and the death clock)
studies.question: How fast must the Boolean NF-kB node follow Lipniacki's nuclear NF-kB (kappa), and how fast is the death machinery (k_time), for the composite's survival / apoptosis / necrosis split under TNF to depend on NF-kB at all?

resolved: Survival under held, saturating TNF is near zero in this composite; Calzone's own network gives 1.4%.
The death clock decides apoptosis against necrosis, and the first fate arrives after about 5-9 Calzone units.
Protein persistence is a lever, capped at fast clocks by production speed (f8).
The readout is alive (never dead), because Calzone's death nodes can switch off again.
Lipniacki's measured protein turnover rate gives none of that lever (f9).
remaining: Whether TNF's dose and timing (exposure, pulse length) change fate, which a held saturating stimulus cannot show.
The death clock still has no measured anchor.

Whether the composite should make death absorbing in the network itself, so that a dead cell stops signalling in the spatial studies (a modelling decision for Alex). Decided 2026-11-06, absorbing (decision 28, f11).
Which part of NF-kB's transient decides fate at 10-30 min per unit, and whether f10's occupancy estimate holds at 120 min per unit; both need the four protective products' states recorded.

followup_study_proposals.title: Graded transcription
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Lipniacki's transcription is proportional to nuclear NF-kB. Calzone's genes see only an on/off node, which is off about 72% of the time at f = 0.28 (f6). Driving the protective products' switch-on rate by f directly would be a coupling change. By f10's quasi-steady estimate it keeps the time-averaged induction (f r_tx) and so the same occupancy; it changes the products' timing, not their average. Its case is fidelity to Lipniacki, not a rescue these data predict (for Alex).

followup_study_proposals.title: Exposure (dose and pulse length)
followup_study_proposals.motivation: With held, saturating TNF, fate is almost fixed, so dose and timing act mostly through whether and when each cell's TNF input switches on, and for how long (u_TNF/d_TNF; McMillan 2021 dose-response, d1).

findings.summary: Alive at 24 h (no death node ever on): 0 at 2, 10 and 30 min per Calzone unit for every kappa. At 120 min per unit it is 6.5% (calzone-flicker), 9.5% (lipniacki-gene) and 16% (lipniacki-nfkb). Durable survival (alive with Survival on at 24 h) is 0.5-4.5% at 120 min per unit and 0 elsewhere. 24 h is only 12 Calzone units at 120 min per unit, short of the 40 at which Calzone's own run is read, so some of those cells may still die.

Near-total death is also Calzone's own answer, but the split is not the same. The unmodified network on the MaBoSS engine (TNF on, cellfate.cfg TransRate 1/24) gives Survival 0.014, Apoptosis 0.953 and NonACD 0.029 at t = 40. At 2 min per unit (effective TransRate r_tx/k_time = 0.039, about 1/25; 24 h is far past t = 40 there) the composite gives no survivor in 600 cells (8 expected at 0.014), apoptosis 0.915-0.95 and necrosis 0.05-0.085 at the end. The difference is the coupling. Calzone's NFkB switches on at rate 1 per unit while its gate is open and stays on. The coupled node switches on at f*kappa and off at (1-f)*kappa even with the gate open (about 9 min to switch on at f = 0.9 and kappa = ln2/337 s, against 2 min for Calzone's at this clock).

Study 0b is confounded and does not test protective-protein persistence. Its edit (decay-lipniacki) also slowed the switch-off of mROS (on when NF-kB is OFF; it licenses ROS, a necrosis driver) and of Survival (the readout node). Cell by cell against the grid: - it changes no cell's alive/dead outcome beyond noise in any pair; - at 2 and 10 min per unit, all six pairs shift the death mode toward necrosis: 9 of 9 changed cells at 2 min per
  unit for both calzone-flicker and lipniacki-nfkb (p = 0.004 each); 15 against 3 at calzone-flicker 10 min per unit
  (p = 0.008);
- at 120 min per unit, where Lipniacki's turnover is 2.2x FASTER than Calzone's switch-off, durable survival at
  lipniacki-nfkb falls from 9 cells to 0 (p = 0.004). Corrected 2026-11-06 (after 0d): it was first read as the
  Survival node decaying faster, but 7 of the 9 die and 2 stay alive with Survival off. 0d, which leaves Survival
  alone, gives the same counts (6 of the 7 dead cells are the same cells), so the faster loss of the protective
  products is enough to cost all 9. 0d does not show that Survival's own faster decay added nothing in 0b.
The p values are uncorrected. None passes a Bonferroni threshold over 48 tests on its own, but the direction is the same in every fast-clock pair, and the mechanism (mROS) is in the edit. Study 0d is the corrected rerun.

The death clock sets the death mode. At kappa = lipniacki-nfkb, end-state apoptosis falls from 0.935 (2 min per unit) through 0.79 and 0.69 to 0.455 (120 min per unit), while necrosis rises from 0.065 through 0.21 and 0.31 to 0.355. The first fate arrives after about 5-9 Calzone units at every clock (medians 18, 74-76, 205-213 and 658-766 min). The median counts only cells with a fate by 24 h, so at 120 min per unit it is biased low.

kappa does not change survival at 2-30 min per unit (no cell alive for any kappa). It moves the apoptosis/necrosis split by up to 0.135 (apoptosis at 30 min per unit). At 120 min per unit, lipniacki-nfkb leaves the most cells alive (16%, against 6.5% and 9.5%). Decision (Alex, 2026-11-06): the composite uses kappa = lipniacki-nfkb (ln2/337 s), the speed measured in Lipniacki's own model, which keeps NF-kB's speed independent of the assumed death clock.

Two regimes, depending on the clock. - Fast clocks (2-10 min per unit). Cells die (medians 18-76 min) before the protective products can be made: they
  switch on at r_tx, a 35-min half-rise, while NF-kB is still in its first wave (f peaks at 0.933 at 24 min). The
  limit is how fast they are made, not how fast they decay. Study 0c supports this: even never-decaying products
  save only 3% at 2 min per unit and 8.5% at 10 min per unit.
- Slow clocks (30-120 min per unit). NF-kB falls to f = 0.020 at 80 min and settles at f = 0.28 after about 6 h. The
  coupled node is then on about 28% of the time, so the protective products' logic keeps failing while the death arms
  run without pause under TNF. Of the cells that show Survival first, 69-100% die later (grid). Study 0c supports
  this too: persistence saves the most cells at the slowest clocks.

Calzone's gates divert death but do not prevent it. Removing caspase-8's cleavage of RIP1 turns every death into necrosis (cell by cell, 158 and 138 apoptotic cells all became necrotic). Removing both gates (that cleavage and SMAC's sequestration of cIAP) leaves every cell dead at some point in 24 h (200 of 200 at 10 and 30 min per unit). The 22-27% that the end state showed as alive had died and then lost the death signal.

Study 0c, an upper bound and not a model: cFLIP, BCL2, mXIAP and mcIAP never switch off once made (kappa = lipniacki-nfkb). Alive at 24 h is 3%, 8.5%, 13% and 33.5% at 2, 10, 30 and 120 min per unit, against 0, 0, 0 and 16% in the grid. Cell by cell, almost every change is dead to alive: 6, 17 and 26 cells saved with none lost at 2, 10 and 30 min (p = 0.031, < 0.001, < 0.001), and 39 saved against 4 lost at 120 min (p < 0.001). Most of the rescued cells have the Survival node OFF at 24 h (durable survival only 0-10.5%), because Survival follows the flickering NFkB node. Alive, not the Survival node, is the readout of a protected cell in this composite.

Study 0d (decay-protective, the corrected 0b; kappa = lipniacki-nfkb): cFLIP, BCL2, mXIAP and mcIAP switch off at Lipniacki's protein turnover rate r_deg = 3e-4/s (A20's c5; half-life 38.5 min, so on average 56 min after their logic fails) at every clock, instead of after one Calzone unit (2, 10, 30 or 120 min). Nothing else is edited. The rate is Lipniacki's; applying it only while the logic fails is the network's form (Lipniacki's decay is constitutive, which would remove the products faster still). Alive at 24 h is 0, 0, 0 and 12% at 2, 10, 30 and 120 min per unit, against 0, 0, 0 and 16% in the grid and 3, 8.5, 13 and 33.5% in the Study 0c bound. Cell by cell against the grid: - at 2-30 min per unit the products take 1.9-28x longer to switch off once NFkB is off, yet 200 of 200 cells die in
  every pair; every cell that 0c saved there dies;
- at 120 min per unit, where the turnover is 2.2x FASTER than the grid's switch-off, 17 cells are newly dead and 9
  newly alive (p = 0.17, no change beyond noise), end-state apoptosis rises from 91 to 103 cells (p = 0.050,
  uncorrected), and durable survival falls from 9 cells to 0 (p = 0.004). Of those 9 grid cells, 7 die and 2 stay
  alive with Survival off (0c keeps 8 of them alive, 3 with Survival on).
Of the cells that show Survival first, all have a death node on later at 2-30 min per unit, and 68 of 86 (79%) at 120 min per unit (grid 59 of 85, 69%; 0c 29 of 87, 33%). The measured turnover rate gives none of the bound's rescue.

findings.summary:
Where the turnover can act depends on the clock. - 2-30 min per unit: 171-200 of the 200 cells in 0d have died before NF-kB settles (6 h), during its first wave
  (f peaks at 0.933 at 24 min), the trough after it (f < 0.1 from 65 to 100 min) and the damped oscillation that
  follows (f 0.2-0.38). At 2 min per unit cells die (median first fate 18 min) before the products are made at all
  (a 35-min half-rise), so their decay cannot matter there. At 10-30 min per unit the bound saves 8.5-13% and the
  measured rate saves none; with no product states recorded, these runs cannot say which part of the transient
  decides that.
- 120 min per unit: 2-4 first deaths (of 133-176 dead cells) come before 6 h, so the settled duty cycle is the
  regime that matters. Quasi-steady, a product's occupancy is f r_tx / (f r_tx + (1-f) r_off): r_tx = 3.3e-4/s
  acts only while the coupled node is on (about 28% of the time; about 11 min on and 29 min off) and r_off only
  while it is off. The grid's r_off = k_time = 1.39e-4/s gives 0.48; 0d's r_deg = 3e-4/s gives 0.30; 0c's r_off = 0
  tends to 1. The order matches durable survival (grid 9 cells, 0d 0, 0c 21) and alive (16%, 12%, 33.5%).
Caveats. The estimate is quasi-steady: the node's phases (11 and 29 min) are not much shorter than the products' time constants (51 and 56 min). The duty cycle is not external: NFkB's logic is IKK AND NOT CASP3, so the death arms close the route the estimate assumes open. Occupancy is not why nearly every cell dies: the 0c bound, with products that stay once made, still kills 87-97% at 2-30 min per unit. Recording the four products' states in a run would test the estimate.
findings.evidence: data/fate-table.json (dead_before_settle, first_survival_then_ever_dead, alive_survival_on_at_end); parquet-runs/grid-lipniacki-nfkb-120min/timeseries.parquet (nfkb_fraction); datasets/calzone2010_cellfate/processed/{transcription_anchor,turnover_anchor}.json (r_tx, r_deg); processed/cellfate_coupled.bnd (cFLIP, BCL2, mXIAP, mcIAP: logic = NFkB, rate_up r_tx; NFkB: IKK AND NOT CASP3)

findings.summary: Absorbing death (decision 28: Apoptosis and NonACD never switch off once on, absorb_death = 1) left the baseline's alive/dead outcome unchanged where it was rerun: on the grid's 200 seeds at kappa = lipniacki-nfkb, 30 and 120 min per unit, no cell's first death moved (0 of 400), the alive set is the same cell for cell (0 and 16%), the first-fate fractions are the same, and no cell revives (120 min per unit: revived 7.5% -> 0, so the end state now equals ever-dead, 0.84). This is observed, not guaranteed: no node's logic reads a death node, but the composite records one sampled joint state per 30 s interval, so a death that switched on and off within one interval can be missed at absorb_death = 0 and recorded at 1 (an earlier recorded death, never a later one). The decay, persist and knockout variants were not rerun; every Study 0 run other than absorb-* used absorb_death = 0. Their recorded document_sha256 values predate decision 28: population.py now writes the death nodes' switch-off as ($absorb_death ? 0 : 1) and sets absorb_death = 0 in each cell's parameters, so a rebuilt document differs from the recorded hash by those two rate lines and that key, while every rate is numerically the same.
findings.evidence: data/paired.json (absorb-*: first_death_tick_differs = 0, ever_dead +0 -0); data/fate-table.json (absorb-*: alive, revived, end_dead, ever_dead); data/absorb-summary.json; checks/boolean/absorbing-death

studies.claim: Under TNF held on at saturation, the coupled composite kills nearly every cell. None is alive at 24 h at 2-30 min per Calzone unit for any kappa, and 6.5-16% at 120 min per unit. Calzone's own network also kills nearly every cell (survival 1.4%), but the coupling shifts that death toward necrosis. Protective products that never decay (Study 0c, an upper bound) leave 3%, 8.5% and 13% alive at 2, 10 and 30 min per unit, and 33.5% at 120 min per unit (grid 16%). Protein persistence is therefore a real lever, but the measured rate does not pull it: with Lipniacki's protein turnover rate on those products (Study 0d, the corrected 0b), 0, 0, 0 and 12% are alive, no alive/dead change beyond noise. At 2-30 min per unit nearly every cell dies before NF-kB settles, during its first wave and the damped oscillation after it. At 120 min per unit the measured turnover is faster than the grid's switch-off and removes the durable survivors.

derived.insight: Alive at 24 h (no death node ever on): 0 at 2, 10 and 30 min per Calzone unit for every kappa. At 120 min per unit it is 6.5% (calzone-flicker), 9.5% (lipniacki-gene) and 16% (lipniacki-nfkb). Durable survival (alive with Survival on at 24 h) is 0.5-4.5% at 120 min per unit and 0 elsewhere. 24 h is only 12 Calzone units at 120 min per unit, short of the 40 at which Calzone's own run is read, so some of those cells may still die.

studies.name: s1-survival-validation
studies.title: Survival under TNF (validation against NF-kB-dependent survival)
studies.question: Under held, saturating TNF, can the composite let most cells with working NF-kB survive, while cells without NF-kB still die, using only the published models' own parameters? If not, where is the limit?

findings.summary: Calzone's network alone, held TNF, t = 40 units, absorbing death, 20,000 trajectories. Alive with NF-kB intact rises with induction speed and saturates: 0.017, 0.078, 0.156, 0.217, 0.242 and 0.252 at TransRate 1/24, 1/4, 1, 4, 16 and 64. Knocked out, no cell is alive at any rate. Survival on is higher (0.014 to 0.319) because in Calzone's network a cell can show Survival and a death node together.

NF-kB's activation route (TNFR -> RIP1 -> RIP1ub -> IKK -> NFkB, four steps) races caspase-8's (TNFR + FADD -> DISC -> CASP8, two steps), and active caspase-8 cleaves RIP1, closing NF-kB's route. Fast induction cannot help a cell whose NF-kB never switches on. In the composite the same race runs on the death clock, because TNFR, RIP1, RIP1ub and IKK switch at k_time (cellfate_coupled.bnd). Read from the rules and the saturation in f1; not tested by varying the upstream rates.

The composite, held TNF from rest, 24 h, 200 cells, at 30, 120, 180, 200, 240 and 480 min per unit. Alive intact against knocked out: 0 and 0; 0.160 and 0.055; 0.465 and 0.340; 0.550 and 0.455; 0.740 and 0.650; 0.980 and 0.985. Rescued against lost by NF-kB: 0/0, 22/1 (p = 6e-6), 36/11 (p = 3e-4), 29/10 (p = 0.003), 26/8 (p = 0.003), 1/2: a net protection of 0, 10.5, 12.5, 9.5, 9.0 and -0.5%. Cells with no fate at all, intact and knocked out: 0/0, 6/11, 43/68, 54/91, 82/130, 163/197. Survival on throughout the last 2 h: 0, 6, 11, 18, 24, 18 cells.

Calzone's network alone at the composite's own settings protects 12.5, 21.5, 17.1, 14.2, 8.8 and 0.3 points at the same six clocks, and its knockouts match the composite's at every clock (0.059 vs 0.055 at 120; 0.339 vs 0.340 at 180; 0.621 vs 0.650 at 240). So the death comes from Calzone's own race (f2), not from the coupling. The coupling lowers protection further at fast and middle clocks (30: 0 against 12.5; 120: 10.5 against 21.5) but not at slow ones. At 200 min per unit most intact cells are alive and most knocked-out cells dead (0.550 against 0.455), which meets the standard only through delay: 54 of 110 alive intact cells reached no fate and 18 held Survival through the last 2 h. No tested clock gives held survival to most NF-kB-competent cells.

studies.claim: Under held, saturating TNF the composite does not meet the standard, read as held survival, at any death clock: NF-kB's net protection is at most about 10-13 points at 24 h, and where most intact cells are alive (200 min per unit and slower) it is because many have not yet reached any fate. The limit is Calzone's own race between caspase-8 and NF-kB's activation route, both on the death clock; the coupling lowers protection further only at fast and middle clocks.
